Sunlight contains all colors (wavelengths). When it enters the atmosphere, it scatters off gas molecules. Shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) scatter much more than longer wavelengths (red/orange) because scattering intensity is proportional to 1/λ⁴. So the blue light is scattered in all directions, making the sky appear blue. Violet scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it and some violet is absorbed by the upper atmosphere.
